exams.name: Data Structures and Algorithms Mid-Semester Proctored Examination
exams.description: Institutional proctored assessment covering coding, reasoning, and algorithmic problem solving under timed conditions.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.prompt: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Each input has exactly one valid answer, and you may not use the same element twice.

questions.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
questions.prompt: You are given an array sorted in ascending order and rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of target if it exists, otherwise return -1. Assume all values are distinct.
constraints: Expected time complexity is O(log n)

questions.title: Longest Valid Parentheses
questions.prompt: Given a string containing only '(' and ')', return the length of the longest valid parentheses substring.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.prompt: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Aim for an O(n) solution using a sliding window.
constraints: s can contain letters, digits, spaces, and symbols

examples.explanation: "abc" is the longest substring without duplicates.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.prompt: You are given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end]. Merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals covering the same ranges.

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.prompt: Given an m x n grid of '1's and '0's, return the number of islands. An island is formed by horizontally or vertically adjacent lands, and the grid edges are surrounded by water.

questions.title: Merge Sort Complexity
questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of merge sort in the best, average, and worst cases?
questions.explanation: Merge sort always splits the array over log n levels and processes n elements per level.

questions.title: Binary Search Tree Property
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes a binary search tree?
options: Every node has exactly two children.
Values in the left subtree are smaller and values in the right subtree are larger.
The tree is always perfectly balanced.
Nodes are stored in insertion order.
questions.explanation: BST ordering is defined by left subtree values being smaller and right subtree values being larger than the node.

questions.title: Hash Map Collision Strategy
questions.prompt: Which technique resolves collisions by storing multiple entries in the same bucket and searching only within that bucket?
questions.explanation: Separate chaining stores colliding keys in a bucket-level collection such as a linked list or dynamic array.
